accuracy.evidence: Every factor checked against the DfE National Curriculum in England (Year 4 measurement: convert between different units of measure, e.g. kilometre to metre, hour to minute; Year 5: convert between km and m, m and cm, cm and mm, g and kg, l and ml) and the SI prefix definitions (kilo = 10^3, centi = 10^-2, milli = 10^-3): 1 km = 1000 m, 1 m = 100 cm, 1 cm = 10 mm, 1 kg = 1000 g, 1 l = 1000 ml; time factors 60, 7 and 12. Every machine answer (3000 m, 400 cm, 2000 g, 60 mm, 5 km, 7 m, 3 l, 8 cm), every pin on the 0–4 km line (2500, 500, 3500, 1750 m) and every time card (120 min, 21 days, 24 months, 240 s, 35 days) recomputed by hand. Parameterised answers 1000*k, c, 60*h, 1000*l, 7*w and n are whole numbers at every corner.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented Year 4/5 slips listed in NCETM's measures guidance and the Ofsted/EEF maths reviews: using 100 for every metric link (the challenge tag hund, the machine's ×100 card for km), multiplying when you should divide and the reverse (the machine names which unit is bigger and whether you need more or fewer), half a kilometre read as 5 m so 3.5 km becomes 3005 m (prediction option, line feedback, mastery m4, tag zero), dividing by 10 instead of 100 so 650 cm becomes 65 m (tag tenx, mastery m8), and converting time in hundreds, 2 hours = 200 minutes (prediction option, the × 100 trap box, mastery m5, tag time).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagconv is built around unit conversion itself: a 1 km road the learner fills with 100 m pieces and must declare complete at exactly 1000 m, a two-way conversion machine with six operation cards (×/÷ 10, 100, 1000) where only the factor-and-direction pair is accepted, a double number line in km and m that snaps to 250 m for pinning 2.5 km, ½ km, 3½ km and 1 km 750 m, and a drag sorter for time conversions with a ×100 trap box. It differs from flagmcalc (same-unit adding), flagunits/flagunit and flagmonths (calendar facts); the gate reports under 30% shingle overlap with every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner meets each rule before the text states it: counting road pieces shows 1 km is ten 100 m pieces; the machine only accepts multiply for big-to-small and divide for small-to-big, and its wrong-answer messages give the reason (more or fewer of the new unit); the double number line makes half a kilometre visibly 500 m, which defeats 3005 m; and sorting time cards shows 60, 7 and 12 instead of 100. Each step ends with a one-line summary only after the task is done.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 100 m in a kilometre (the road needs ten pieces), dividing or 'adding zeros after the point' for 3 km to m (the machine accepts only × 1000), 700 cm giving more metres (the machine shows 7 m), 3005 m or 350 m for 3½ km (the pin lands at 3500 on the line), and 200 or 260 minutes in 2 hours (the ×60 box and the ×100 trap). The task message echoes the locked-in choice.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with two wrong options each, every one mapped to its own message: hund (kilo is 1000, not 100), same (km is the bigger unit, multiply), tenx (divide by 100, not 10: 6.5 not 65), mulw (to a bigger unit you divide), zero (half a kilogram is 500 g, not 5 g), time (time is not in hundreds), div (minutes are smaller, so multiply by 60) and add (6 weeks is 6 lots of 7, not 6 + 7). In-lab mistakes also name the slip, e.g. '1 m is 100 cm, not 1000. Use × 100.'

readability.evidence: validate_lessons.py passes the learner limits (kid FK under 6.5, adult under 9.5). Kid paragraphs are short and concrete ('Big unit to small unit? You need more of the small ones, so multiply.'), and the precise curriculum words for Year 4–5 are used: kilometre, metre, centimetre, millimetre, kilogram, gram, litre, millilitre, convert, multiply, divide.

no_filler.evidence: No filler pattern matches. Each lab step has one job (the size of a km, big to small, small to big, decimals, time) and every feedback line carries a number or a rule. Item explanations show the calculation and the reason (bigger unit, so divide) instead of restating the question.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px in light and dark theme on every step after Show me. First pass fixes: the unit facts on the road step overlapped the feedback box and were moved up; pin labels on the number line collided at 1750 and 2500 m, so only the latest pin is labelled and a 'Pinned:' row lists the rest; time-card results overflowed the narrow ×60/×7 boxes and now sit in a two-column list under the boxes. The six operation cards are 3 per row and about 40 px tall, and all canvas actions are repeated by full-size buttons.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button: 'Add 100 m', 'That makes 1 km', six ×/÷ buttons with labels such as 'Multiply by 1000', '◀ 250 m' / '250 m ▶' / 'Pin at 2500 m' for the number line, and one button per multiplier for the time cards. The canvas aria-label states the state after each move ('Change 700 cm into m. Pick an operation.', 'Road: 600 metres of 1 kilometre.'). Challenge feedback is an aria-live status. walk.cjs reports axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors; the canvas keeps a light card in dark mode.
